**Setup.** Place the regular heptagon on the unit circle (circumradius $1$) with center $O$ at the origin, and vertices at angles
$$A=0,\ B=\tfrac{2\pi}{7},\ C=\tfrac{4\pi}{7},\ D=\tfrac{6\pi}{7},\ E=\tfrac{8\pi}{7},\ F=\tfrac{10\pi}{7},\ G=\tfrac{12\pi}{7}.$$

**Locating $P$.** Since $PA=PB$, point $P$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of chord $AB$, which is the ray from $O$ through the midpoint $M$ of $AB$, i.e. the ray at angle $\pi/7$. We have $|OM|=\cos(\pi/7)$ and $|AB|=2\sin(\pi/7)$. Since $\triangle PAB$ is equilateral with side $|AB|$, its height is $\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}|AB|=\sqrt3\sin(\pi/7)$, so
$$|PM|=\sqrt3\sin(\pi/7),\qquad |OP|=|OM|-|PM|=\cos(\tfrac{\pi}{7})-\sqrt3\sin(\tfrac{\pi}{7}).$$
(The other equilateral vertex lies outside the heptagon; this one, with $|OP|>0$, is inside.) Set $r:=|OP|$.

**Key identity.** Since $\tfrac{\pi}{42}=\tfrac{\pi}{6}-\tfrac{\pi}{7}$,
$$2\sin(\tfrac{\pi}{42})=2\Big(\tfrac12\cos\tfrac{\pi}{7}-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin\tfrac{\pi}{7}\Big)=\cos\tfrac{\pi}{7}-\sqrt3\sin\tfrac{\pi}{7}=r.$$

**Collinearity of $P,O,E$.** Vertex $E$ sits at angle $\tfrac{8\pi}{7}=\tfrac{\pi}{7}+\pi$, i.e. on the ray opposite to $P$ through $O$. Hence $P,O,E$ are collinear with $O$ between $P$ and $E$, so the ray $PE$ coincides with the ray $PO$. Therefore
$$\angle CPE=\angle OPC.$$

$$\angle POC=\tfrac{4\pi}{7}-\tfrac{\pi}{7}=\tfrac{3\pi}{7}.$$
Thus $\angle OPC+\angle OCP=\pi-\tfrac{3\pi}{7}=\tfrac{4\pi}{7}$.
